subject: Azure Private Plan: licensing transition & co-sell transition playbook
messages:
From: Meredith Cole <procurement@lumenhealth.com>

Cc: Alan Bower <alan.bower@lumenhealth.com>, procure_ops@lumenhealth.com
Date: Sun, 5 Dec 2027 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: Azure Private Plan: licensing transition & co-sell exhibit questions

Naomi — thanks for the overview last week. As we review the Private Plan term sheet with our legal and procurement teams we have two items that need clarification before we can route for internal approval: 

1) Royalty / co-sell exhibit: your term sheet references a "royalty" for marketplace-originated seats. Can you confirm whether this is intended to be a revenue share for Azure co-sell referrals, or a per-seat royalty? Our procurement team prefers a clear, capped referral fee tied to the HubSpot opportunity rather than an ongoing royalty tied to product licensing.

2) Licensing transition: LumenHealth needs a clear migration path if we later move from Redwood-hosted to a Dedicated/Private deployment (e.g., IP/compiled model rights, data export windows, support SLA during migration). The draft has high-level language but not the operational steps or timelines.

I've attached our RFP response and a redline template. Can you send an updated term sheet or proposed exhibit language we can review with Alan by Wednesday? Also please include any standard DocuSign flow for co-sell scenarios so we can estimate procurement lead time.

Thanks,
Meredith
Procurement Manager
LumenHealth

Attachments: Lumen_RFP_response_v3.pdf

Meredith — really appreciate the clear asks and the RFP. Linking in Jonas (Solutions Eng) to confirm technical migration steps and Irene (Legal) to propose concrete exhibit language for co-sell/referral.

Quick answers up front:
- We intended the marketplace "exhibit" to be a referral fee model (one-time payout tied to origin) rather than a per-seat royalty. That said, we can cap fees and tie them to opportunity IDs in HubSpot as you request.
- We have a standard migration playbook for Hosted -> Private that includes export windows (30 days data extraction), support overlap (2-week dedicated on-call), and an intake checklist. Jonas will paste the operational checklist below.

Next steps:
1) Irene will propose redline text for a "Co-Sell / Referral Exhibit" and a short licensing transition paragraph.
2) Jonas will confirm the migration timeline and any additional costs or prep work.
3) If that looks good, I'll prepare a DocuSign envelope with the term sheet + exhibit so you can route internally.

Onward —
Naomi
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Azure Private Plan: licensing transition & co-sell exhibit questions — proposed redlines

Meredith / Alan — looping in a short set of proposed redlines for the "Co-Sell / Referral Exhibit" and a concise "Migration & Licensing Transition" paragraph for the term sheet. I tried to keep language operational and Azure-compliant (marketplace does not allow unreconciled perpetual royalties in many cases). Please see the two suggested clauses below; if acceptable we can insert these verbatim into the term sheet and I will provide a tracked-change .docx.

Proposed: "Co-Sell / Referral Exhibit" (summary):
- Definition: "Marketplace Originated Opportunity" means a customer opportunity created in the Azure Marketplace or identified in HubSpot with an opportunity ID referenced in the DocuSign envelope.
- Fee: Redwood shall pay a one-time referral fee equal to 10% of the first twelve months' Redwood invoiced net revenue for Marketplace Originated Opportunities, capped at $250,000 per opportunity. No ongoing royalties beyond the first-year payout.
- Payment Timing: Fees paid within 45 days of Redwood's receipt of customer payment and reconciling invoice. Redwood will provide a quarterly reconciliation report to Azure and the partner.

Proposed: "Migration & Licensing Transition":
- Export and Handoff: Upon written request, Redwood will provide customer data export (standard formats for metadata, vectors, and content) within 30 days of request.
- Technical Support During Migration: Redwood will provide a 2-week migration support window at no additional cost to assist with KV cache seeding, model conversion notes, and validation tests. Extended migration engineering support will be available under a Statement of Work.
- IP/Model Rights: Nothing in this agreement transfers Redwood's underlying model IP. Customer receives the exported artifacts and any deployed configuration required to run their private deployment, subject to standard license restrictions documented in Appendix A.

Operational checklist (Jonas — feel free to refine):
- Confirm target private deployment region and instance types
- Snapshot current model version and tokenization configs
- Export customer prompts, eval sets, and KV cache prefixes where requested
- Schedule 2-week overlap window with platform on-call
- Run smoke tests and sampling for latency/throughput targets

If LumenHealth prefers a different fee structure (flat referral fee or lower %), we can negotiate — the principal constraints are Azure marketplace rules and our internal commercial guardrails.

If folks are aligned, Naomi can cut a new term sheet and I will prepare tracked redlines.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Naomi / Irene / Jonas — thank you for the rapid turn. The proposed referral exhibit and migration paragraph align with what our stakeholders expected. A couple of small asks before legal will sign-off: 

- Can we reduce the referral fee cap to $150,000 for scaled enterprise deals? That keeps the one-time nature but reduces the exposure for very large purchases.
- Please add a short sentence to the migration paragraph: "Redwood will retain audit logs of export activity for 90 days post-export and provide export confirmation receipts."

Assuming those tweaks, procurement is ready to accept and route for signatures. Our internal timeline: we will seek PO approval next week and aim to execute within two weeks after DocuSign. Please go ahead and send the final term sheet + exhibit via DocuSign with HubSpot opportunity ID prefilled: HS-OPP-29821.

Next steps (from our side):
- Alan will do a final contractual review by Thursday.
- Procurement will raise PO after DocuSign execution.

Meredith
